{"world_model":"W6 after E052. Time ≈ 0.1 s fixed + steps × per-step cost. Per-step cost is pixel-proportional compute plus a bandwidth-bound part (BN/GELU/pointwise, ~27% of a 32 px step). Tip E049: 5.198 s, 0.7535 on seeds 0–2. E052 (selection + top-up on E049) read 4.987 s and 0.7555. Seeds 0–2 accuracy is noise-limited, about ±0.3 pp across rebuilds of identical code (E036 vs E050 etc.). The population mean is ~0.752–0.753, so the bar is only barely cleared.

Mechanisms and support:
1. Accuracy rises slowly with optimizer steps, about 1.5–2.5 s/pp. Pure step, epoch and sample cuts trade near the dial (E020, E031, E040, E041, E037, E045, E048). E052 shows selection plus top-up is at least dial-neutral.
2. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 32 px tail and the 3×3 final-map regime carry accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
3. Late backward truncation saves more than its MAC share, because frozen blocks also skip BN/GELU backward, optimizer updates and Lookahead traffic (E028, E034, E036, E046, E049). Late freezes are roughly neutral; early freezes are not (E037's cliff, which suggests the stem needs time at 32 px). Each added freeze yields ~0.1–0.2 s. Extending the group-2 freeze from 10% to 15% should save about 0.08–0.15 s at ~0.05–0.1 pp cost.
4. Averaging, LS, warm-up, Lookahead-interval, BN-recalibration and batch-split tweaks are null or negative. The recipe is near a local optimum.
5. Math-identical systems work is worth 1–2% each (E035). Only ~2.5% of GPU time is outside the step graphs (E047).
6. wd ×0.5 helped ~0.2 pp (E016).
7. Architecture surgery on high-resolution work (E051: stride-2 stem) loses accuracy faster than it saves time, ~0.3 s/pp, far worse than the dial.
8. Elementwise work is bytes-bound. ReLU might save 1–3% of time; the accuracy effect is probably -0.1 to -0.3 pp.
9. Build-to-build kernel reselection moves 3-seed accuracy by up to ~0.3 pp. Time noise is ±0.04 s.

Misses: truncation and selection savings keep beating my estimates (E041, E046, E048, E052). Accuracy on identical code swings ±0.3 pp. My time ranges were too high-centered for stacked-trim ideas; widen them downward.

W6 after E052. Time ≈ 0.1 s fixed + steps × per-step cost. Per-step cost is pixel-proportional compute plus a bandwidth-bound part (BN/GELU/pointwise, ~27% of a 32 px step). Tip E049: 5.198 s, 0.7535 on seeds 0–2. E052 (selection + top-up on E049) read 4.987 s and 0.7555. Seeds 0–2 accuracy is noise-limited, about ±0.3 pp across rebuilds of identical code (E036 vs E050 etc.). The population mean is ~0.752–0.753, so the bar is only barely cleared.

Mechanisms and support:
1. Accuracy rises slowly with optimizer steps, about 1.5–2.5 s/pp. Pure step, epoch and sample cuts trade near the dial (E020, E031, E040, E041, E037, E045, E048). E052 shows selection plus top-up is at least dial-neutral.
2. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 32 px tail and the 3×3 final-map regime carry accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
3. Late backward truncation saves more than its MAC share, because frozen blocks also skip BN/GELU backward, optimizer updates and Lookahead traffic (E028, E034, E036, E046, E049). Late freezes are roughly neutral; early freezes are not (E037's cliff, which suggests the stem needs time at 32 px). Each added freeze yields ~0.1–0.2 s. Extending the group-2 freeze from 10% to 15% should save about 0.08–0.15 s at ~0.05–0.1 pp cost.
4. Averaging, LS, warm-up, Lookahead-interval, BN-recalibration and batch-split tweaks are null or negative. The recipe is near a local optimum.
5. Math-identical systems work is worth 1–2% each (E035). Only ~2.5% of GPU time is outside the step graphs (E047).
6. wd ×0.5 helped ~0.2 pp (E016).
7. Architecture surgery on high-resolution work (E051: stride-2 stem) loses accuracy faster than it saves time, ~0.3 s/pp, far worse than the dial.
8. Elementwise work is bytes-bound. ReLU might save 1–3% of time; the accuracy effect is probably -0.1 to -0.3 pp.
9. Build-to-build kernel reselection moves 3-seed accuracy by up to ~0.3 pp. Time noise is ±0.04 s.

Misses: truncation and selection savings keep beating my estimates (E041, E046, E048, E052). Accuracy on identical code swings ±0.3 pp. My time ranges were too high-centered for stacked-trim ideas; widen them downward.

Unsure: the true tip mean, the selection bias, transfer to the PCIe judge, how far the group-2 freeze can extend, and whether intermittent stem backward is neutral.

forecasts.reason: Longer group-2 freeze saves ~0.1 s; the accuracy cost is within noise of 3 seeds.
Same change as I082 but against a same-build E049 baseline; the result is noise-limited.
Skipping stem backward on half of the 28 px steps saves ~0.1 s; the accuracy effect is uncertain and small.
The freeze moves only 4% earlier, saving ~0.05 s; the cliff question is not resolvable on 3 seeds.
A profiling gate: probably the projected saving is under 3% and it closes with no run; if run, the effect is small.
Stacked trims plus top-up give ~3–4% less time at roughly neutral accuracy, within noise.

cruxes: Is the tip's true population mean (seeds 13–32) above 0.7525, or is the 0.753–0.755 reading selection bias? This decides how much margin remains for further trims.
Does the group-2 freeze dose have a cliff like the group-1 freeze at 60% (E037), or does it scale linearly to 15–20%?
Does ReLU's bandwidth saving reach 3% of train time, and is its accuracy cost under 0.15 pp?
